thread:
olivia: heads-up — support escalated a customer (ACME Corp) about p99 latency spikes on model `text-gen-v2` in us-west-2 starting ~2026-03-15T12:30Z. p95 also up. customer sees timeouts in their UI. attaching metrics they sent and our dashboard snippets.

aaron: seen this on the dashboards too. p99 went from ~450ms -> ~1.8s across the last 30m. p95 moved from 300ms -> ~620ms.

maria: logs show an increase in tail queue wait times on the inference pods. a lot of reqs hitting 2nd-stage batching. kernel-side mem spikes on a subset of hosts. possible KV cache pressure?

zoe: @olivia can you paste the repro curl or the request shape they use? helps narrow if it's a long prompt or big context.

olivia: here's the simplified repro they gave (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"text-gen-v2","input":"<~1.2k tokens prompt>","max_tokens":512,"temperature":0.2}' \
  --max-time 8
```

sam: thanks. long prompt + 512 max_tokens will definitely amplify tail latency. also their traffic is bursty (seen short bursts of 40-60 r/s). combined with batching it's plausible.

aaron: quick checks I ran:
- PromQL: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))` -> jumped to ~1.8s in us-west-2 12:30-12:55
- pod CPU/IO: a small subset of pods show 90-100% GPU util, rest are ok
- autoscaler kept up but batch queue depth increased

maria: also seeing a spike in `kv_cache_miss_rate` around same window. could be working set thrash when many distinct prompts cause cache churn.

olivia: customer's impact: UI timeouts at 3s, partial responses, retries. they're asking for immediate mitigation and an ETA.

aaron: immediate mitigations (5-15m):
1) apply per-customer rate limit -> 10 rps burst (throttle) on ACME route via Console (temporary).
2) enable model fallback rule for that customer to `text-gen-v2-compact` (lower latency but slightly lower quality).
3) set circuit breaker: fail fast after 800ms for non-streaming requests (return 429 with `x-retry-after`).
4) reduce max batch size from 32 -> 8 for us-west-2 pool to cut tail.

zoe: agree. also we should route priority customers to dedicated pool if they have dedicated capacity. ACME doesn't. so fallback + rate limit is quickest. I'll draft the customer message.

maria: I'll investigate infra side for root cause while you do mitigations. focusing on host set where kernel OOM/GC looked noisy.

aaron: I'm going to open runbook steps and apply rule 1 & 3 now.

deploy-bot: deploy request created by aaron for route-rule change: RR-2026-309. CI checks passed.

aaron: applied per-route throttle at the control plane. confirming metrics now.

maria: looking at host 10.12.4.22 — GPU driver reported a transient reclaim and we had higher memcpy latency to host memory. kernel log snippet:
```
Mar 15 12:31:22 host kernel: NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00.0: Xid (GPU crash) 79, pid=0: RENDER_ERROR: 0x63e17
Mar 15 12:31:22 host kernel: oom_reaper: reaped process 21452 (inference-worker) total-vm:1420128kB
```

zoe: ugh. GPU Xid and OOM signs. could be a buggy kernel + stress combo with large inputs.

sam: confirm customer-side: they paused retries and we see reduced retries. p95/p99 trending down after throttle + fallback.

olivia: customer update (sent): "We're applying a temporary throughput cap and routing some of your requests to a lower-latency model to stabilize response times. We'll follow up with RCA/ETA." they replied :thumbsup:.

aaron: next quick tweak: enable model fallback routing for all requests with prompt > 800 tokens OR estimated output > 400 tokens. adding rule now.

deploy-bot: config change deployed: MODEL-FALLBACK-2026-42 by aaron.

maria: long-term notes (repo/infra items):
- investigate kernel/driver versions on problematic hosts, plan rolling upgrade to stable driver.
- add SIGSEGV/Xid alerting to detect GPU repro quickly.
- expand KV cache capacity and add eviction metrics per model so we can detect working set thrash.

zoe: operations playbook draft (to put in runbooks/incoming-latency):
1) triage: confirm p95/p99 delta and affected regions/models. gather sample requests.
2) immediate mitigations: a) per-customer throttles, b) circuit breaker at 800ms, c) fallback to compact model or other region, d) reduce max batch size for pool.
3) infra remediation: cordon/replace noisy hosts, check GPU driver logs, scale dedicated pools for high-SLA customers.
4) post-mortem: collect kernel logs, driver versions, batch-queue histograms, KV cache miss rates, and customer request samples.

aaron: adding SLO guardrails suggestion:
- auto-enable circuit-breaker when p99 > 1.2s for 2 consecutive 5m windows per region-model pair.
- auto-fallback to compact model when avg tokens/request > 600 for more than 5m.
- per-customer burst-limit default 20rps, can be lowered dynamically when tail latency > threshold.

sam: good. also add a safety route: route a small percent (5%) to a different region (us-west-1) as automatic geographic fallback when we detect region-level tail regressions.

maria: creating INC-2026-042 for this. I'll attach host kernel dumps and list of affected pods.

oncall-bot: incident created: INC-2026-042 — latency spike us-west-2 — assigned to oncall @maria.

zOE: (typo in name) sorry, small note: include customer impact classifications in runbook: P0 (timeouts affecting >5% requests), P1 (>1% users impacted), etc. helps prioritize dedicated pool migration.

olivia: after mitigations p95 back to ~320ms, p99 ~620ms. still elevated but manageable. customer is ok with follow-ups.

aaron: follow-ups for next 48h:
- maria: RCA and host driver upgrade plan (ETA 24h)
- aaron: add auto-circuit rule to staging for 1 day experiment (ETA 4h)
- zoe: publish playbook and customer-facing summary (ETA 2h)
- sam: monitor for regressions and validate fallback quality for sample prompts (ETA 6h)

sam: I'll also add a synthetic load test for long prompts to our nightly suite so we can catch similar regressions in pre-prod.

olivia: thanks team. good recovery. keeping INC open until RCA complete. :rotating_light:

(oncall-bot pinned: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-042)
